name: Town Square
fact: The first word search was published in 1968 in a small newspaper in Norman, Oklahoma.
alt: Paper-cutout town square with a brick clock tower, a striped-awning bakery and cosy cottages

name: Eiffel Tower
fact: It was built for the 1889 World’s Fair in Paris and stands about 330 metres tall today.
alt: Paper-cutout Eiffel Tower in daylight above Paris rooftops and the river Seine

name: Venice Canal
fact: Venice is built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon, linked by around 400 bridges.
alt: Paper-cutout row of pastel Venetian houses over a turquoise canal with a gondola and striped poles

name: Cyclades Village
fact: The Cyclades are about 220 islands in the Aegean Sea. Their name comes from the circle they form around Delos.
alt: Paper-cutout white cube houses with blue domes on a cliff above the deep blue Aegean and a sailboat

name: River Nile
fact: At about 6,650 km, the Nile is one of the longest rivers on Earth. Wooden feluccas have sailed it for centuries.
alt: Paper-cutout felucca with a tall white sail on the Nile at sunset, palms, a mud-brick village and camels on the dunes

name: Amboseli Savanna
fact: From Amboseli you can see Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa’s highest peak at 5,895 metres, just across the border in Tanzania.
alt: Paper-cutout snow-capped Mount Kilimanjaro above golden savanna with acacia trees, giraffes and elephants

name: Taj Mahal
fact: Emperor Shah Jahan built it in memory of Mumtaz Mahal. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
alt: Paper-cutout Taj Mahal with its minarets, reflecting pool and cypress-lined garden

name: Floating Market
local: ตลาดน้ำ · Talat Nam
fact: Damnoen Saduak, one of Thailand’s best-known floating markets, grew along a canal dug in the 1860s.
alt: Paper-cutout floating market with wooden boats full of fruit and flowers, sellers in straw hats, stilt houses and palms

name: Mount Fuji
fact: At 3,776 metres it is Japan’s highest mountain. It joined the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2013.
alt: Paper-cutout Mount Fuji with a snow cap, a calm lake, a red bridge and cherry blossoms

name: Great Wall
fact: Built and rebuilt over many centuries, it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
alt: Paper-cutout Great Wall winding over green mountain ridges with watchtowers and autumn trees

name: Twelve Apostles
fact: Waves from the Southern Ocean carved these limestone stacks out of the cliffs. Despite the name, there were never twelve.
alt: Paper-cutout limestone sea stacks standing off ochre cliffs in the Southern Ocean at dusk

name: Diamond Head
fact: Sailors in the 1800s mistook shiny calcite crystals on this old volcanic crater for diamonds, which gave it its English name.
alt: Paper-cutout Diamond Head crater above a curving beach with palms, surfboards and an outrigger canoe

name: Fiesta Plaza
fact: Papel picado means “pierced paper”. Artisans cut lacy patterns into tissue paper to decorate streets for fiestas.
alt: Paper-cutout sunny plaza with pink, yellow and turquoise adobe houses, papel picado banners, cacti and marigolds

name: Rainbow Mountain
fact: Vinicunca rises more than 5,000 metres high in the Andes. Its colourful stripes are layers of different minerals.
alt: Paper-cutout striped Rainbow Mountain in red, ochre, turquoise and lavender with snowy Andes peaks and llamas

name: Sugarloaf Mountain
local: Pão de Açúcar · Rio de Janeiro
fact: Sugarloaf rises about 396 metres above Guanabara Bay. Its cable car first opened in 1912.
alt: Paper-cutout Sugarloaf Mountain rising from Guanabara Bay with a cable car, sailboats, a beach and palms

name: Horseshoe Falls
fact: The Horseshoe Falls is the largest of Niagara’s three waterfalls, and most of it lies on the Canadian side.
alt: Paper-cutout curved Horseshoe Falls with mist, a rainbow, a small tour boat and red and orange maple trees

name: Statue of Liberty
fact: A gift from the people of France, it was dedicated in New York Harbor in 1886.
alt: Paper-cutout Statue of Liberty on its island in the harbor with a ferry and a distant skyline

name: Northern Lights
fact: Iceland’s best season for the northern lights runs from about September to April, when the nights are long and dark.
alt: Paper-cutout green and violet northern lights over snowy mountains, a black sand beach and a red-roofed cabin

name: Edinburgh Castle
fact: The castle sits on Castle Rock, the plug of a volcano that erupted about 350 million years ago.
alt: Paper-cutout grey stone castle on a high volcanic rock above old town rooftops and purple heather

name: Emperor Penguins
fact: Emperor penguins are the tallest penguins, up to about 1.2 metres. They raise their chicks through the dark Antarctic winter.
alt: Paper-cutout emperor penguins and a chick on an ice shelf beside tall blue-white icebergs and a low polar sun
